name: Polar cold traps
basis: Radar-bright craters at the poles that never see the Sun hold water ice; MESSENGER neutron measurements found it in a layer tens of centimetres under a dark cover, in quantity far above the planet's dry surface. Grade is relative.

name: Northern smooth plains
basis: Volcanic plains of magnesium-rich basalt. MESSENGER measured sulfur up to about 4 percent by mass, ten times Earth's crust, and potassium high enough that the planet is volatile-rich rather than depleted. Grades are relative.

name: Intercrater plains
basis: The old cratered terrain between the large basins, the same magnesium-rich rock with somewhat less sulfur. Grades are relative.

name: Atmosphere
basis: A 92 bar atmosphere of 96.5 percent carbon dioxide and 3.5 percent nitrogen, with a cloud deck of sulfuric acid droplets at 48 to 60 km and sulfur dioxide at trace level. Carbon dioxide and nitrogen keep their proportions; the acid and sulfur grades are estimates. Known from probes and spectroscopy.
